title: Document dev->main promotion mechanics in the release runbook
description: Follow-up from QCLI-332 (0.8.0 release prep), suggested by opum-agent: the release runbook (docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md) never documented how dev is promoted to main, which is why QCLI-332's own acceptance criteria didn't name that step. Three release-blocking-looking-but-actually-fine signals were learned executing the 0.8.0 promotion and would otherwise be re-derived under time pressure by the next releaser: two full rounds of required checks fire on one dev-to-main PR's head SHA, promotion-is-manual/main-is-fast-forward-of-dev are a documented always-fail tripwire not a blocker, and mergeStateStatus reads UNSTABLE on this PR shape by design.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A "Promoting dev to main" section exists in docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md documenting: promotion is orthogonal to the numbered release steps (release.yml dispatches against the tag, never main), the two-rounds-of-required-checks behavior on a dev->main PR head SHA, the promotion-guardrails tripwire jobs, mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE being expected, and the origin/dev:main push convention
lore sync and lore check both exit 0 on the change

implementationNotes: Added the 'Promoting dev to main' section to docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md (between step 8 and the darwin-arm64 SIGKILL-hazard section), covering the three signals learned executing the QCLI-332 0.8.0 promotion: two rounds of required checks fire on one dev->main PR head SHA (verified live via the ruleset-intersection query during that promotion), promotion-is-manual/main-is-fast-forward-of-dev are the documented always-fail tripwire from promotion-guardrails.yml, and mergeStateStatus reads UNSTABLE on this PR shape by design. lore sync regenerated docs/log.md (1 entry added, committed alongside); lore check exits 0 (63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings). Landed via branch docs/QCLI-334-promotion-runbook-section -> PR #187.
finalSummary: Added a 'Promoting dev to main' section to docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md, capturing three signals learned live during the QCLI-332 0.8.0 promotion that otherwise read as a broken promotion mid-release: two full rounds of source-gates/Tracker integrity/lore check fire on one dev->main PR head SHA, promotion-is-manual failing and main-is-fast-forward-of-dev skipping are promotion-guardrails.yml's documented always-fail tripwire rather than blockers, and mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE is expected on this PR shape. lore sync/lore check both exit 0. Landed via PR #187 rather than a cross-session message, per opum-agent's point that a message dies with the session but the runbook is what a releaser has open in the moment those signals appear.
